titulo: Quiz — Τον λογαριασμό — nothing arrives without being asked
subtitulo: The banned cover charge, the compulsory list, and whose job the receipt is
introPt: A traveller closes a meal: asks for the bill, queries a line nobody offered, and takes the printed paper.
cenario: The end of dinner on a terrace, with bread on the table that arrived on its own.

dialogo.es: Τι είναι αυτό; Το ψωμί δεν το ζητήσαμε.
dialogo.pt: What is this? We didn't ask for the bread.
dialogo.tts: Τι είναι αυτό; Το ψωμί δεν το ζητήσαμε.

dialogo.es: Έχετε δίκιο, συγγνώμη. Το βγάζω αμέσως.
dialogo.pt: You're right, sorry. I'll take it off right away.
dialogo.tts: Έχετε δίκιο, συγγνώμη. Το βγάζω αμέσως.

perguntas.pergunta: A cover charge — κουβέρ — appears on your bill in Greece. What is the position?
opcoes: It is lawful if written on the menu, as in Italy
It is lawful only outside the tourist season
It is prohibited outright
It is lawful up to two euros per person
perguntas.explica: Article 72 of the ΔΙ.Ε.Π.Π.Υ. rules bans it. Greece runs the opposite logic to the Italian coperto, which is lawful when declared.

perguntas.pergunta: Bread and bottled water land on the table without anyone asking you. Can they be charged?
opcoes: Yes, they are standard table items everywhere
No — nothing may be served and charged without prior consent
Only the water, never the bread
Only if the total is above twenty euros
perguntas.explica: Bread and bottled water are named explicitly in the rule. The fine is €500 per item. Bread may be charged only where it was offered and accepted.

perguntas.pergunta: What does the law require about the price list?
opcoes: It must exist somewhere on request
It must be in Greek, visible at the entrance and again before you order, with tax included
It must be posted in Greek and English
It is only required for businesses with outdoor seating
perguntas.explica: Articles 70 and 71. No list at all is a €1,000 penalty; a price charged above the listed one is €500 per item.

perguntas.pergunta: Whose legal obligation is the printed receipt?
opcoes: The customer's — you can be penalised for leaving without it
The business's, under Law 4308/2014
Nobody's; it is a courtesy
The customer's, but only for amounts above €50
perguntas.explica: Issue through a certified fiscal device has been required since 1 January 2015. The claim that a customer can be penalised has no located basis.

perguntas.pergunta: What percentage should you tip in Greece?
opcoes: Ten per cent
Fifteen per cent at dinner
Five per cent, rounded up
No documented percentage exists — do the mechanics and round up
perguntas.explica: Tipping is recognised enough for a 2024 law to exempt up to €300 a month from income tax, but no survey or federation produces a figure. Any number quoted online is a guess.
